quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: When a school bus has its lights flashing and its stop arm extended, you must:

options.text: Stop at least 10 feet away from the bus.
Pass if children have exited the bus.
Stop if the bus is on the opposite side of a barrier.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at least 10 feet away from the bus.
questions.explanation: When a school bus flashes red lights and extends its stop arm, you must stop at least 10 feet away. The only exception is if the bus is stopped on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These actions take your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. Drivers who do these things have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicles.

questions.question: Checking your blind spot by turning your head before changing lanes, leaving a curb, or merging is:

options.text: Not necessary if you use the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder toward the next lane before changing lanes. Do not rely only on your mirrors.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is:
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
You may proceed if the way is clear.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you see this sign, you are going the wrong way. You risk a head-on collision. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights are working properly.

questions.explanation: Nighttime driving is harder because you cannot see as well. Take steps to make night driving safer for yourself and others on the road.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, remember:

options.text: Roads are especially slippery right after it starts to rain.
Give yourself extra space to stop.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after rain starts. Wet pavement is covered with a layer of oil, dirt, and water. Slow down in heavy rain, standing water, or slush to keep your tires from losing grip.

questions.question: If a police officer requires you to take a blood, breath, or urine test, you:

options.text: May choose which test you prefer.
Must take the test or your license will be suspended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must take the test or your license will be suspended.
questions.explanation: If you are arrested for driving under the influence and refuse a chemical test of breath, blood, or urine, your license will be suspended for one year. This suspension happens even if you are found not guilty.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Begins to metabolize itself more quickly.
Decreases the number of driving errors.

questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reactions, makes you feel more confident, and causes you to make more errors.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: To turn safely, activate your turn signal three to four seconds before you turn.

questions.question: If a police officer stops you, what should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Have your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel. Wait for the officer to come to you.
Get out of your car and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car with your hands on the steering wheel. Wait for the officer to come to you.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the wheel when stopped by police. Tell passengers to keep their hands visible too. Stay in your car unless the officer tells you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your driver license, registration, and insurance cards.

questions.question: How does lack of sleep affect your driving compared to other factors?

options.text: The same way driving with teenagers does.

questions.explanation: Tiredness and alcohol affect your driving ability in similar ways. Being awake for 18 hours impairs your driving about as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.05%. Being awake for 24 hours impairs your driving about as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.10%.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you cannot see cross traffic clearly. What should you do?

options.text: Roll down your windows, listen for traffic, then go.
Move forward slowly to see clearly. Check for traffic and pedestrians. Go when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward slowly to see clearly. Check for traffic and pedestrians. Go when the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign where you cannot see cross traffic, yield to pedestrians. Then move forward slowly past the stop line until you can see clearly. Check for traffic and pedestrians. Go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: A police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light. What should drivers do?

options.text: Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic lights help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists must obey traffic signals. The only exception is when a police officer is directing traffic. Then you must follow the officer's directions.

questions.question: Which of these distractions increases crash risk for drivers?
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone (including hands-free phones) or audio devices (radio or CD player) can distract you from driving and increase crash risk.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, what should you do?

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on slippery roads is always dangerous, especially on turns and curves. Slow down more than usual when taking turns in slippery conditions.

questions.question: When sharing the road with a truck, remember that trucks generally:

options.text: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on a downhill slope than smaller vehicles.
Need a smaller turning radius than smaller vehicles.
Need less time to pass on an uphill slope than smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
questions.explanation: Trucks are larger and heavier than smaller vehicles. Because of this, they need longer distances to stop.

questions.question: You see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and give them the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.
